nav.title: Project settings
nav.notAdmin: Only project admins can change settings. Ask an admin of {{project}} if something needs changing.

details.title: Details
details.burndownHint: Both feed the project burndown in the backlog.
details.privateHint: Off makes it public: anyone can view it and find it in Discover.
details.lookingForPeopleHint: Shows in Discover that the project wants contributors.
details.contactableHint: People outside the project can send the admins a message from Discover.

logo.title: Logo
logo.description: Square images work best. PNG, JPEG or GIF.

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: Turn parts of Kemudi on or off for this project.
modules.epicsHint: Group stories into larger pieces of work.
modules.kanbanHint: A board of stories by status.
modules.wikiHint: Pages for the team’s shared knowledge.

duplicate.title: Duplicate
duplicate.description: Start a new project with this one’s settings, statuses, roles and custom fields.

transfer.title: Transfer ownership
transfer.description: The new owner gets an email and must accept. Until then you stay the owner.

delete.title: Delete project
delete.description: Deletes every story, task, issue, epic, wiki page and attachment in it. This cannot be undone.
delete.typeName: Type the project name to confirm.

members.title: Members ({{total}})
members.description: Roles decide what members can see and change. Admins can also change these settings.

pending.title: Invitations waiting ({{total}})
pending.description: These people have not accepted yet.

remove.title: Remove {{name}}?
remove.description: They lose access to the project. Their stories, tasks and comments stay.

invite.title: Invite people
invite.description: People with an account join at once; others get an email to sign up.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Every member has one role. Roles that count for points get their own estimate on each story.
roles.moveMembers: Members with this role move to:

public.title: Outside the team
public.description: This project is public. Choose what people outside it can see and do.
public.signedIn: Signed-in people who are not members
public.anonymous: Visitors who are not signed in

storyStatuses.title: Statuses
storyStatuses.description: The columns of the kanban and the steps a story goes through.

points.title: Points
points.description: The values people can estimate a story with.

storyDueDates.title: Due date warnings
storyDueDates.description: Highlight stories this many days before they are due.

taskDueDates.title: Due date warnings
taskDueDates.description: Highlight tasks this many days before they are due.

issueStatuses.title: Statuses
issueStatuses.description: The steps an issue goes through.

issueTypes.title: Types
issueTypes.description: Kinds of issue, such as bug or question.

priorities.title: Priorities
priorities.description: How soon an issue should be dealt with.

severities.title: Severities
severities.description: How bad the effect of an issue is.

issueDueDates.title: Due date warnings
issueDueDates.description: Highlight issues this many days before they are due.

epicStatuses.title: Statuses
epicStatuses.description: The steps an epic goes through.

values.closedHint: Items in this status count as done
values.archivedHint: Hidden from the kanban unless archived is shown
values.removed: It is removed from this project.

customFields.deleteDescription: Its values are deleted from every item.

tags.description: Rename a tag everywhere, give it a colour, merge duplicates, or delete it from every item.
tags.empty: No tags yet. They appear here once items use them.
tags.deleteDescription: It is removed from every story, task, issue and epic.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Kemudi POSTs a JSON event to each URL whenever a story, task, issue, epic, sprint or wiki page changes. The key signs each request (X-TAIGA-WEBHOOK-SIGNATURE, HMAC-SHA1).
webhooks.deleteDescription: Kemudi stops sending events to this URL.

intro.title: Commits and issues from code hosting
intro.description: Mention an item in a commit message to link it, and add a status to move it: TG-12 #done closes item 12 with the status whose slug is done. Issues opened on the code host can create Kemudi issues too.

services.github: Repository settings, Webhooks: content type application/json, the secret below, events "push", "issues" and "issue comment".
services.gitlab: Project settings, Webhooks: the URL below (it carries the key), triggers "push", "issues" and "comments".
services.bitbucket: Repository settings, Webhooks: the URL below, triggers "repository push" and issue events.
services.gogs: Repository settings, Webhooks: content type application/json, the secret below.

integrations.originIps: Accept hooks only from these addresses
integrations.originIpsHint: IP addresses or ranges (CIDR), separated by commas. Empty accepts any.

export.title: Export
export.description: A full copy of the project (items, comments, attachments, settings) as a Taiga export file. Import it into Kemudi or Taiga to restore or move the project.
export.started: Export started. You get an email with the download link when it is ready.

feeds.title: CSV feeds
feeds.description: A secret link per list that always downloads the current data as CSV, for spreadsheets and reports. Anyone with the link can read it; make a new link to cut off the old one.

sprintAccess.title: Sprint access
sprintAccess.description: Limit a role to some sprints. Its members then see only those sprints, and the stories, tasks and issues in them; the backlog stays visible. Project admins always see everything.
sprintAccess.empty: This project has no sprints yet.
